To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a hypervalent iodine(III) reagent, PhI(OH)X (X = BF(4), OTf), is a new and efficient fluorinating agent for the monofluorinating reaction of benzene ring of 3-arylpropyl ethers in the presence of 18C6, BF(3), and water.
the para-selective aromatic monofluorinations of 3-arylpropyl ethers have been developed using a novel iodosylbenzenemonomer·18-cROWN-6 complex [PPhI(OH)(BF(4))·18-cROWN6].
3-phenethyl ethers are fluorinated in high yield and with good para-selectivity by a hypervalent iodine-mediated process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the synthesis of fluorinated organic compounds.
the development of a new method for the regioselective fluorination of aromatic compounds.
the synthesis and application of hypervalent iodine reagents, especially iodosylbenzenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reaction of 3-arylpropyl ethers with [PhI(OHBf(4))·18-crown 6] and BF(3)-OEt(2) in the presence of water at room temperature provides a new method for the regioselective para-monofluorination and direct preparation of 3-(4-Fluorophenylethyl)propyl Ethers in good yields.
the hypervalent iodine-mediated fluorination is a powerful tool for the preparation of fluorinated aromatic ethers and is a promising method for the synthesis of fluorinated aromatic compounds.
the hypervalent phenyliodane-mediated para-fluorination of benzyl ethers has been achieved for the first time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hypervalent phenyl iodane-mediated aromatic fluorination is the first example to realize the direct para-selective monosubstitution of benzene ring by the neighboring group effect.

the neighboring alkoxy groups in 3-phenypropyl ethers are able to participate in the aromatic fluorination of the benzene ring and the resulting 4-fluorobenzene ring would be directly converted into the corresponding 3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)propyl ether.
the neighboring group participation is a powerful tool for the para-selective fluorination of aromatic rings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neighboring alkoxy effect is not restricted to the neighboring hydroxyl group.
the para-fluorination reaction of 3-arylpropyl ethers is a new and useful synthetic method for preparing 3-(4-substituted phenyl)propyl ether derivatives.
this protocol is a simple, efficient, and environmentally benign method for the preparation of 4-fluorinated phenyl ethers.
